why: PolicyLink is Next's own documented hover-prefetch pattern written out line by line, and every Link the brief names sits at the stated line; the rest is a tag swap in twelve files that touches no money, sign-in or data. The type check, the nav unit tests (which compare markup) and the whole signed-in e2e project catch a dropped attribute, a broken LinkPending or a link that stops navigating. A wrong edit costs only slower or faster prefetching, which is easy to see in the network panel and to revert.
harm_if_wrong: Admin links would prefetch too much or not at all, or the new spec would guard nothing, with no effect on data or permissions.
brief_problems: vitest.config includes only src/**/*.test.ts, so src/components/policy-link.test.tsx would never run and the commit 1 check that names it finds no test; the brief should name policy-link.test.ts with React.createElement outright.
The hover case says 'at most 2' new prefetch requests but not 'at least 1', so a spec whose request detector matches nothing passes every row at 0; add 'at least 1, for /admin/{store}/products'.

e2e/prefetch.spec.ts and src/lib/cross-root-links.scan.test.ts come from step 0.12 and do not exist yet; the focus-frame line 36 edit leaves a choice ('policy none … or keep Link') that depends on how 0.12 wrote its rule.

The six non-zero ceilings and every row's `fetches` list are whatever the first run prints, so they are recorded rather than checked, and the exact fetch lists (notices poll, speed beacon) may make the spec flaky.
